title: Design Parking System
description:
# Design Parking System

Design a parking system for a parking lot. The parking lot has three kinds of parking spaces: big, medium, and small. The number of available spaces for each size is fixed when the object is created.

Implement the `ParkingSystem` class:

* `ParkingSystem(int big, int medium, int small)` initializes the number of big, medium, and small spaces.
* `boolean addCar(int carType)` tries to park one car. `carType` is `1` for a big car, `2` for a medium car, and `3` for a small car.

A car may only use the matching space type. If a matching space is available, occupy exactly one such space and return `true`. If no matching space remains, leave the system state unchanged and return `false`.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example 1

**Input**
["ParkingSystem", "addCar", "addCar", "addCar", "addCar"]
[[1, 1, 0], [1], [2], [3], [1]]

**Output**
[null, true, true, false, false]

**Explanation**
`ParkingSystem parkingSystem = new ParkingSystem(1, 1, 0);`
`parkingSystem.addCar(1);` returns `true` because one big space is available.
`parkingSystem.addCar(2);` returns `true` because one medium space is available.
`parkingSystem.addCar(3);` returns `false` because there are no small spaces.
`parkingSystem.addCar(1);` returns `false` because the only big space has already been occupied.

## Constraints

* `0 <= big, medium, small <= 1000`
* `carType` is `1`, `2`, or `3`.
* At most `1000` calls will be made to `addCar`.

solutions.name: Array Remaining Slots
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store the remaining big, medium, and small slots in a three-element array. Because `carType` is `1`, `2`, or `3`, the matching index is always `carType - 1`.

## Key Insight
The operation only changes one counter. Check the selected counter first; if it is zero, return `false` without touching any other type. Otherwise decrement that counter and return `true`.

## Complexity Analysis
Each `addCar` call performs a constant number of array operations, so the time complexity is O(1) per operation. The array always has length three, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Explicit Fields And Branches
solutions.description:
## Approach
Keep three named fields: `big`, `medium`, and `small`. In `addCar`, branch on `carType` and update only the field that represents the requested space size.

## Key Insight
This version favors readability over indexing. It makes the state transition for each car type explicit, which is useful when teaching design problems with a very small fixed set of states.

## Complexity Analysis
The method checks at most three branches, so each operation runs in O(1) time. The object stores three integer counters, so the extra space is O(1).

solutions.name: Map Backed Capacity
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store the remaining capacity for car types `1`, `2`, and `3` in a map. Each call reads the value for the requested `carType`, rejects zero capacity, and writes back one less slot after a successful park.

## Key Insight
A map models the car type as a key instead of as an array index. This is more general than needed for three types, but it teaches the common design pattern of mapping operation parameters to mutable state buckets.

## Complexity Analysis
The map has only three entries, so each lookup and update is O(1) for this problem. The stored state is fixed-size, so the extra space is O(1).

solutions.name: Capacity And Occupied Counters
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store the original capacity in one array and the number of occupied spaces in another array. A parking attempt succeeds only while `occupied[index]` is strictly smaller than `capacity[index]`.

## Key Insight
This route uses the dual view of the state: instead of decreasing remaining slots, it increases used slots. It produces the same behavior but helps learners see that either remaining capacity or used capacity can represent the invariant.

## Complexity Analysis
Each call performs one index calculation, one comparison, and possibly one increment, so the time complexity is O(1). Both arrays have fixed length three, so the space complexity is O(1).
